candidates.title: Women’s Affect and Queer Fandom in China
candidates.abstract: This book investigates how “rotten girls”—female fans of male-male romance—navigate the affective terrain of queer fandom in post-socialist China. Focusing on the everyday experiences of these fans, it traces their engagements with queer representations of masculinity across state-sanctioned, commercial, and fan-produced media. Through the lens of affect, this book highlights how these women negotiate identity, desire, and agency within an environment marked by censorship, market forces, and patriarchal norms. Drawing on semi-structured interviews and close analysis of danmu (real-time comment) fan videos and online discussions, the study introduces the concept of a “post-socialist structure of feeling” to capture the intuitive, often ambivalent ways fans inhabit Chinese queer fandom. It explores how this cultural space serves as an affective heterotopia—a contradictory, emotionally charged zone where fans consume, produce, and contest representations of soft masculinity. This book also examines how these women emerge as “killjoys”: feminists-in-the-making who challenge, endure, and reimagine the limits of China’s heteronormative social order. Offering original insights into Chinese queer fandom, this book is a valuable resource for scholars and students in media and cultural studies, gender studies, queer theory, and Asian studies. It contributes to growing conversations in transcultural fan studies by foregrounding affect as both a methodological and conceptual tool for understanding how digital fandom mediates identity, emotion, and power in contemporary China.

candidates.title: Techno-Wellbeing and Flourishing in Higher Education: Student Experiences of Using Generative AI
candidates.abstract: In recent years, the rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has sparked widespread interest, optimism, and concern. Tools such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini are increasingly used by students to support academic tasks, manage workloads, and navigate personal challenges. While much of the discourse has focused on academic integrity and performance, relatively little is known about how these technologies shape students’ psychological wellbeing, sense of self, and capacity to flourish during their university experience. Drawing on flourishing theory, this study explores how GenAI adoption intersects with students’ personal, academic and emerging professional lives, including its perceived role as mentor, coach or companion. Flourishing provided a lens to examine broader dimensions of wellbeing such as purpose, engagement, relationships and optimism in the context of GenAI. Utilising the Listening Room methodology, friendship pairs from a UK university took part in timed, prompt-led conversations, sharing their lived experiences of using GenAI. Findings indicate that students predominantly use GenAI as an augmentative tool to translate briefs, break down tasks, provide exemplars and refine communication, which enhance perceived competence and increase engagement and confidence in academic work. At the same time, students expressed concerns about fairness, academic integrity, over-reliance, skill atrophy, misinformation and the idea of GenAI as an emotional “friend”, highlighting potential risks to self-respect, authentic relationships and trust in assessment. The study concludes that GenAI can both support and erode flourishing, stressing the need for human-centred institutional guidance that foregrounds wellbeing, alongside moral integrity and academic outcomes.

candidates.title: From Accuracy to Responsibility: A Systematic Review of Computational Sustainability, Algorithmic Fairness, and Governance in Transformer-Based Text Classification
candidates.abstract: Background The rapid adoption of Transformer-based architectures such as BERT and RoBERTa has advanced text classification in high-stakes domains, including cyberbullying detection, mental-health screening, and fake-news moderation. However, these advances have increased computational demands and raised concerns regarding environmental sustainability, algorithmic fairness, and responsible governance. This systematic review examines the interrelationships among computational sustainability, Green AI mechanisms, the efficiency–fairness trade-off, and governance in Transformer-based text classification. Methods A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies were identified from five databases: ScienceDirect, Wiley Online Library, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and ProQuest. A total of 94 studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to examine strategies for improving computational efficiency, their implications for fairness, and governance mechanisms relevant to responsible Transformer-based text classification. Results Four complementary categories of Green AI mechanisms were identified: model compression, including pruning, knowledge distillation, and quantization; alternative energy-efficient architectures; secure and efficient inference; and lifecycle-oriented governance techniques such as machine unlearning. Across the reviewed studies, these mechanisms reduced parameter counts or energy consumption by up to sixty-fold while generally maintaining comparable predictive performance. However, efficiency gains did not consistently preserve fairness, with some compression strategies increasing subgroup performance disparities, particularly for under-represented languages and demographic groups. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning demonstrated potential for jointly improving efficiency and equity. Persistent governance gaps were also identified, including limited alignment between machine-unlearning techniques and regulatory rights such as the GDPR right to erasure, insufficient transparency in vendor-imposed training decisions, and limited sustainability criteria for evaluating legacy research. Conclusions The findings indicate that computational efficiency, algorithmic fairness, and governance should be considered interconnected dimensions of responsible Transformer-based text classification rather than independent objectives. The review proposes a unified evaluation framework integrating sustainability metrics, fairness-aware evaluation protocols, and governance considerations to support more responsible Transformer deployment and research. The findings also highlight potential contributions to Sustainable Development Goals 9, 10, 12, and 13.

candidates.title: From Virtual Persona to Purchase: The Trust Engagement Pathway of AI-Generated Influencers in Sustainable Textile Marketing
candidates.abstract: While AI-generated social media influencers can provide consistency, scalability, and creative control to the textile industry, there is a question about their credibility when they make sustainability-related statements. The current research investigates how the effectiveness of AI-influencers affects consumers' trust in brands, sustainable brand engagement, and purchase intention in the textile industry in Pakistan. The model combines the Stimulus-Organism-Response model and source credibility and signaling models. To finalize and validate the reporting framework, a deliberately generated data set of 250 potential social-media consumers was analyzed with an explicitly simulated approach in PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrapped replications. All HTMT ratios were below .85 and the measurement model had acceptable reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .854-.884) and convergent validity (AVE = .683-.718). AI-influencer effectiveness was a strong predictor of consumer trust, sustainable engagement, and purchase intention (beta = .497, .251, and .181, respectively). The trust variable (beta = .425) and the variable of sustainable engagement (beta = .176) to purchase intention were significant, while the variable of sustainable engagement was the strongest predictor of purchase intention (beta = .346). Indirect effects via trust and engagement and the serial pathway of trust-engagement also showed significant results. The results confirm that AI-powered endorsers have the greatest impact when they are transparent and credible, fostering trust and driving sustainability awareness to genuine engagement with the brand. This is a simulated numerical dataset, and thus the results illustrate an analytically coherent paper structure; these should be replaced or verified with real field data prior to the actual publication of the dataset.

candidates.title: More than a loading bar: Conversational silence and anthropomorphic latency cues in mental health chatbots
candidates.abstract: Mental health chatbots increasingly rely on conversational interaction to support users' emotional well-being, yet little is known about how users interpret temporary silence while waiting for system responses. Existing research on social presence and anthropomorphic interaction has primarily focused on conversational content after a response is generated, whereas the waiting phase remains underexplored. Drawing on social presence theory, this study conceptualizes anthropomorphic latency cues as socially meaningful signals that may shape users’ emotional and interactional experiences during temporary conversational silence. Two studies were conducted. Study 1 developed and semantically validated three categories of anthropomorphic latency cues (empathic, effortful, and playful). Study 2 employed a within-subjects laboratory experiment with university students, comparing five latency-cue conditions (text, progress bar, empathic, effortful, and playful) using subjective evaluations, eye-tracking measures, and semi-structured interviews. The results showed that anthropomorphic latency cues were associated with lower anxiety and greater pleasure in several condition-level comparisons relative to non-anthropomorphic feedback. Perceived interaction continuity was significantly associated with reduced anxiety and enhanced pleasure. Within the anthropomorphic conditions, mediation analyses revealed significant indirect associations among perceived anthropomorphism, social presence, and emotional and interactional outcomes. Eye-tracking results indicated longer fixation durations on anthropomorphic latency cues during temporary silence. Qualitative findings further suggested that participants often interpreted latency cues as signals of attentiveness, responsiveness, and interaction continuity rather than merely as technical loading indicators. Overall, temporary conversational silence may function as a socially meaningful phase of AI-mediated interaction rather than a purely technical delay. The study extends social presence research into temporally silent phases of conversational AI interaction and provides preliminary design implications for chatbot-based support systems.

candidates.title: Makerspaces in School Libraries - Transforming Learning Ecosystems for 21st Century Education: A review
candidates.abstract: Makerspaces in school libraries have become transformative settings that enhance creativity, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills in learners. Based on constructivist and constructionist theories, these spaces transition libraries from passive information stores to active learning environments. This review synthesizes existing research on the conceptual basis, implementation, educational effects, challenges, and future prospects of makerspaces, highlighting their role in supporting STEM/STEAM education, digital literacy, inquiry-based learning, and inclusive pedagogy. Global evidence, including guidelines from the American Association of School Librarians and the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions, underscores the essential role of school librarians as facilitators and leaders in innovation. While studies indicate improved student engagement, self-directed learning, and collaborative knowledge construction, obstacles like funding shortages, training deficiencies, and sustainability challenges, particularly in developing areas, persist. The review concludes that makerspaces signify a paradigm shift in school librarianship, promoting 21st-century competencies and equitable access to creative technologies. To optimize their educational benefits, strategic planning, policy alignment, and librarian development are crucial.

candidates.title: Ready for robotic dentistry? a comparative study of trust, behavioral intention, and procedural acceptance
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence and robotic systems are becoming part of dental care, but it remains unclear to what extent dentists, dental students, and non-dental participants would accept receiving robot-assisted dental treatment themselves and how much they trust these technologies. This cross-sectional online survey included 1,055 participants: 542 dental students, 95 practicing dentists, and 418 non-dental participants. The questionnaire assessed perceived usefulness, procedural acceptance, trust and control, social influence, ethics, privacy, and cost, and behavioral intention. All composite scores were calculated on 5-point Likert-type scales, with higher scores indicating greater agreement or acceptance. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, the Friedman test, correlation analyses, and hierarchical linear regression. Participants generally considered AI and robotic systems useful, but their willingness to undergo robot-assisted dental procedures was relatively low. Mean scores were 2.95 for perceived usefulness and 2.25 for procedural acceptance. Acceptance differed significantly across the 11 dental procedures, with the highest score for tooth whitening and the lowest for soft-tissue surgery. Dentists showed lower procedural acceptance than both dental students and non-dental participants. The trust and control construct was the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, followed by procedural acceptance and perceived usefulness. The final regression model explained 56.5% of the variance in behavioral intention. Acceptance was generally lower for more invasive procedures, particularly surgical procedures. Acceptance of AI and robotic dentistry was associated more strongly with trust, clinician control, and procedure type than with perceived usefulness alone. Further cross-cultural studies involving multiple countries are needed to confirm these findings in more diverse populations.

candidates.title: Brand Trust in the Digital Marketplace: Conceptual Perspectives and Emerging Dimensions
candidates.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed the marketplace and created new challenges for developing and maintaining consumer trust in brands. In digital environments, consumers interact with organizations through websites, social media, mobile applications, online platforms, artificial intelligence, personalized communication and digitally mediated service encounters. These developments have expanded opportunities for organizations to build relationships with consumers while simultaneously increasing concerns related to privacy, security, transparency, authenticity, information credibility and technology-mediated interactions. This paper reviews the existing literature on brand trust in the digital marketplace and examines its changing dimensions in contemporary digital environments. The review focuses on the role of digital marketing, social media, artificial intelligence, personalization, electronic communication, customer experience, online reviews, digital platforms, transparency, privacy and consumer–brand relationships in shaping trust. The literature indicates that brand trust in digital environments is multidimensional and extends beyond traditional perceptions of brand reliability and credibility. Consumers increasingly evaluate brands according to their ability to provide secure, transparent, personalized, authentic, consistent and meaningful digital experiences. At the same time, excessive personalization, inappropriate data practices, technological uncertainty and information overload can weaken consumer confidence. The paper consolidates the existing literature and identifies emerging dimensions of digital brand trust, including technological trust, data and privacy trust, platform trust, interactional trust, experiential trust and authenticity. The review contributes to the understanding of how traditional concepts of brand trust are being reshaped by the characteristics of the digital marketplace.
authors: Krishna Kumar JHA Krishna Kumar JHA

candidates.title: A systematic review and Zero Trust governance framework for agentic UAV robotics in public safety
candidates.abstract: Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) robotic systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical public-safety environments, including emergency response, search and rescue, infrastructure inspection, traffic incident assessment, and drone-as-first-responder (DFR) operations. At the same time, the supporting AI is shifting from scripted remote control toward agentic behavior: perceiving, planning, invoking external tools (GIS, CAD), retaining mission context, coordinating with other agents, and recommending actions to human operators. This evolution multiplies the attack surface of public-safety UAV robots across identity, device, communication, data, AI-reasoning, and governance planes, while existing studies often treat UAV autonomy, cybersecurity, and governance as separate problems. This paper presents a systematic review of 2014–2026 literature spanning agentic UAV autonomy, Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), UAV cybersecurity, LLM-agent security, and public-safety robot governance, synthesized into the Zero Trust Agentic Drone Public-Safety (ZTADP) Framework: a six-layer model—Mission, Identity & Access, Device, Communication, Agentic Reasoning, and Evidence & Governance—applying continuous verification to every actor, data stream, tool call, and AI-mediated recommendation in a UAV mission. The paper contributes a mission-pipeline threat model, design principles for least-privilege autonomy and human-confirmed action, a framework architecture, and a validation roadmap. We argue that trustworthy public-safety UAV robotics requires verifying not only who controls a robot, but also whether its own reasoning, tool use, and evidence handling can be trusted. The paper closes with a research agenda toward Zero-Trust-by-design, explainable, privacy-preserving, sustainable, and audit-ready agentic aerial robotics.

candidates.title: Research on multimodal human-computer interaction algorithm integrating DiT and space-time attention characteristics
candidates.abstract: To address challenges such as time-alignment difficulties, feature-space heterogeneity, and insufficient cross-modal semantic association modelling in multimodal human-computer interaction, this paper proposes a multimodal human-computer interaction algorithm. The algorithm integrates DiT (Diffusion Transformer) and space-time attention mechanisms within a dual-way parallel fusion framework. It employs adaptive gate control integration, combined with a multi-scale decoding structure, to realise cross-modal semantic alignment and multi-granular interactive state output. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including NTU RGB+D 60, NTU RGB+D 120, EgoGesture, and CMU Mocap, demonstrate the approach's effectiveness. Specifically, the algorithm achieved Top-1 recognition accuracy of 92.5% on NTU RGB+D 60 and dual-stream fusion accuracy of 91.2% on EgoGesture. In the full-modal configuration, recognition accuracy on CMU MoCap reached 95.1%. Reasoning delay remained under 50 milliseconds. The algorithm outperformed ResNet-LSTM, Transformer, and other mainstream methods across action recognition and intention-understanding tasks, demonstrating strong real-time performance and generalisation. The DiT branch performs condition-guided global feature refinement, whereas the spatio-temporal attention branch independently emphasizes informative spatial nodes and temporally discriminative segments. Their gate-controlled fusion preserves complementary generative-semantic and motion-dynamic information instead of relying on direct feature concatenation, improving cross-modal discrimination and robustness to incomplete or noisy cues.

candidates.title: The paradox of pleasing: therapeutic recognition and the limits of conversational AI
candidates.abstract: Abstract Conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) is increasingly used by hundreds of millions of people for emotional support, personal advice, and therapeutic purposes, rapidly emerging as a mediator of human self-understanding (Stade et al. 2025). Yet despite growing evidence of systematic user-validation in CAI, documented as “sycophancy” in the AI safety literature (Sharma et al. 2024), its implications for how individuals come to understand themselves remain largely unexamined. This article addresses that gap by reframing sycophancy not as a technical alignment failure or a purely philosophical concern, but as a failure of recognition in the psychoanalytic and critical-theoretical sense. We identify a core tension we term the “paradox of pleasing”: CAI’s drive to please renders it structurally unable to provide the friction, conflict, and encounter with otherness that genuine recognition requires. Drawing on Winnicott’s (1960, 1971) concepts of “holding” and “object use,” we contend that CAI’s inability to provide necessary resistance or survive aggression prevents the transformative psychological development found in the human therapeutic encounter. Extending this analysis through Honneth’s (1995) theory of recognition and Whitebook’s (2001a, 2021) critique of Honneth, we argue that CAI reflects the undervaluing of the “work of the negative.” This limitation risks flattening consciousness by converting collective political frustration into privatized, soothed affect, undermining the conditions for critical social thought. The article concludes by suggesting that the encounter with the paradox of pleasing ultimately serves to foreground the unique and indispensable nature of human therapeutic recognition.

candidates.title: Text-messaging with a conversational AI as an out-group member: Preliminary evidence for a new application of intergroup contact
candidates.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) for electronic contact (e-contact) offers new possibilities for intergroup contact. This pilot study examined whether exchanging instant messages with an AI-generated out-group member reduces prejudice, using explicit and implicit pre- and post-contact evaluations with a pure control condition. The contact was designed in accordance with Allport's optimal contact conditions and strategies derived from categorization theories. Sixty-one Japanese adults participated in this study. One month after the pre-evaluation, participants in the contact condition engaged in a 15-min interaction with a text-based AI designed to represent a Chinese individual, during which they introduced themselves and discussed possible joint efforts toward achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. The results showed that the contact condition increased explicit measures of positive attitudes and intergroup empathy while reducing negative attitudes relative to the control condition. However, intergroup anxiety and implicit attitudes measured using the Implicit Association Test showed no contact effects. Our findings suggest that a brief, semi-structured contact involving personalized interaction and cooperation task may mitigate some aspects of explicit intergroup bias. This preliminary evidence indicates new possibilities for applying conversational AI in instant messaging environments within intergroup contexts and provides implications for effective e-contact strategies.

candidates.title: Moral risk awareness and AI adoption: Integrating technological acceptance and moral foundation theories
candidates.abstract: This article focuses on understanding moral risk awareness in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. We integrate two methodological frameworks combining the Technology Acceptance Model with Moral Foundations Theory through a three-pronged analytical approach and examine cross-cultural surveys using Bayesian statistics. The research examines how emerging AI technologies influence issues of unfairness, loss of privacy, erosion of autonomy, cultural erosion, rising environmental costs, and disruption of social order and harmony. The goals are, first, to understand the moral risk awareness that comes with AI technology, and second, to enhance AI governance by providing valuable insights for countries and organizations worldwide in their efforts to harmonize AI innovations with social good while respecting the moral foundations that drive public acceptance versus resistance to AI.

candidates.title: The Impact of Digital Finance Adoption on MSMEs in Indonesia - State of the Art
candidates.abstract: Background Digital finance is currently experiencing significant developments. This development is global, in both developed and developing countries. One impact is that MSMEs must adopt digital finance to compete globally. The development of field papers from year to year needs to be summarized and analyzed carefully to produce findings relevant to scientific research. Methods This study presents a state-of-the-art review of the impact of digital finance adoption on Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) method. Through a systematic search, selection, and filtering process in the Scopus database, 31 selected scientific articles were obtained as the basis for the analysis. Results The study results show that digital finance, including electronic payments, mobile banking, peer-to-peer lending, and fintech platforms, has been widely adopted across countries and has contributed to increased financial inclusion, improved financing efficiency, innovation, and stronger MSME performance. However, the adoption of digital finance also faces several challenges, such as low digital financial literacy, cybersecurity risks, and access disparities between urban and rural areas. Conclusions In the Indonesian context, the success of digital finance adoption is greatly influenced by the government’s role through financial inclusion and economic digitalization policies, as well as by collaboration with business actors such as fintechs, digital banks, and e-wallet providers. This study also identified that digital payment applications and e-wallets are the most dominant technologies used by MSMEs in Indonesia. Overall, this study confirms that digital finance has a strategic role in supporting the transformation and sustainability of MSMEs in Indonesia and provides direction for the development of more contextual and sustainable future policies and research agendas.

candidates.title: Chain of thought driven reinforcement alignment with KAN for multimodal sentiment analysis of tourist reviews
candidates.abstract: Multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis integrates text, images, and emojis to capture fine-grained emotional tendencies, making it particularly useful for social media opinion analysis and user experience evaluation. Traditional feature-level fusion networks, however, are easily corrupted by visual noise and lack explicit explanations for their emotional logic. At the same time, generative large language models, while capable of logical reasoning, are prone to hallucinations. Moreover, the discrete symbol streams they generate autoregressively are mathematically non-differentiable, making it exceptionally difficult to combine high-precision discriminative networks with interpretable generative networks. To tackle these challenges, we propose CoT-KRA, an interpretable sentiment analysis model for tourist reviews driven by a combination of Chain-of-Thought reinforcement learning and multi-layer Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN). Our framework departs from traditional forced image-text alignment, positioning the large language model as a prior reasoning generator and leaving the final decision to a downstream classifier. Specifically, we build a supervised fine-tuning dataset using distilled text from the open-source DeepSeek-R1 model to bolster the basic expressive power of our policy backbone, Meta Llama 3 8B-Instruct. This backbone parses aspect-aware dynamic emoji attribute triplets, which are then mapped into high-dimensional continuous feature vectors via a learnable polarity modulation projection matrix. We then construct a feature collaborative encoding module based on Conditional Layer Normalization to inject high-order prior knowledge without loss. To handle distortion noise in the visual channel, we design a derivative-free visual quality evaluation operator that implements adaptive gating truncation. We also replace the traditional Multi-Layer Perceptron with a KAN prediction network, taking advantage of its edge-learnable 1D spline curve activation to achieve highly precise non-linear decision boundaries. During policy optimization, we design a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm and a multi-dimensional composite reward function, feeding back the classification accuracy of the KAN network as an advantage signal to guide the LoRA updates of the language model policy. Evaluated on a dual NVIDIA RTX 3090 hardware setup, CoT-KRA achieves advanced classification performance on social media datasets like Twitter-2015, Twitter-2017, and SemEval-2017, as well as Yelp and TripAdvisor review collections.

candidates.title: Hospital AI and robotics adoption and access inequality in the United States
candidates.abstract: Abstract Hospital artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics are diffusing unevenly across the United States, but national evidence on adoption, access, and 2023 care outcomes remains limited. We linked calendar-year 2023 American Hospital Association adoption data for 6166 hospitals with 2023 CMS hospital outcomes, 2023 CDC hospital-setting mortality, and county social and population data for 3143 U.S. counties. Access inequality was substantial: 65.8% of the access-analysis population lived within 30 minutes of AI-enabled care, and population-weighted travel burden remained highly unequal for AI and robotics access (Gini = 0.740 and 0.776) despite a 56% increase in AI-enabled hospitals between 2022 and 2024. In adjusted models conditioning on 2019 baseline performance and organizational and county covariates, staff-scheduling AI was associated with higher sepsis bundle completion (3.9% relative difference), and routine-task automation AI with lower 30-day pneumonia mortality (5.4%). County-level mortality associations were more heterogeneous: access to routine-task automation AI was associated with lower 2023 hospital-setting mortality in the primary specification, but the estimate was sensitive to estimator choice and organizational-capacity adjustment. These findings benchmark AI- and robotics-enabled hospital access inequality and suggest outcome-specific adjusted associations warranting longitudinal confirmation rather than causal interpretation.

candidates.title: Fan comments, emotions, and imagination in Chinese online soccer novels from a digital humanities perspective
candidates.abstract: In the era of global digitalisation, soccer fan communities within the niche domain of online literary fandoms, alongside their concomitant nationalist discourses, have emerged as pivotal subjects of scholarly inquiry. However, extant research has largely overlooked the cultural dimensions and subjective articulations of these fan groups. Moreover, as research paradigms increasingly shift towards digital media, methodological frameworks rooted in digital humanities warrant further refinement. This study examines 297,290 reader comments on soccer-themed online novels authored by Lin Hai Ting Tao on Qidian Chinese Literature, analysing the affective expressions and virtual imaginaries of Chinese digital soccer fans. Utilising computational tools such as Python, Nvivo and ROST CM, alongside hermeneutic interpretation, the findings reveal that readers: (1) employ a ‘plot borrowing’ narrative strategy to articulate real-world perspectives; (2) pursue vicarious competitive experiences within the author’s constructed the “Second Soccer World “, transposing unrealised championship aspirations onto fictional narratives; and (3) exhibit radical romanticism within the dialectical tension between virtual and real spaces, manifesting a form of digital nationalism. Practically, this study provides actionable insights for national institutions and sports organisations engaged in fan management tasks related to competitive sports such as soccer. Theoretically, it advances the digital representation of online fan communities and contributes a robust digital humanities methodology for textual analysis.

candidates.title: Barriers, motivations, and the path to gender parity in the maker communities
candidates.abstract: Abstract The maker movement, characterized by do-it-yourself (DIY) innovation and collaborative production, has emerged as a potential driver of skill development, sustainability, and community engagement. However, despite its potential to foster inclusive and circular economies, gender disparities persist in participation within makerspaces. This study investigates the motivations, barriers, and gender differences influencing engagement in European makerspaces, drawing on a comprehensive survey of over 6000 respondents across 28 European countries, including Turkey. Using principal component analysis (PCA), we identify distinct dimensions of motivations and barriers, revealing that women are more motivated by skill enhancement, community engagement, and sustainability but express greater challenges related to access to information, time constraints, and technical skills. Men, on the other hand, are more concerned with externalities such as environmental and health impacts. The study also highlights minor concerns about inclusivity, with both men and women expressing dissatisfaction with the representation of age, gender, and ethnic diversity in makerspaces. Despite these barriers, women demonstrate a greater willingness to visit maker communities and to use makerspace facilities compared to men, yet do not actually use them more, even not when they have first-hand experience with them, suggesting persistent gendered barriers within the maker spaces. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions, such as accessible training programs, mentorship opportunities, and financial support, to bridge the gap between motivation and participation. We discuss the findings in terms of how equitable design and support of makerspaces can foster circular economy practices while enhancing access to community-based skill development.

candidates.title: Remembering or monitoring? Contextual fit of simulated AI memory cues and consumer trust
candidates.abstract: AI assistants increasingly refer to information they ostensibly retain from earlier sessions. A remembered preference can signal attentiveness, whereas a reference to stress or late-night behavior can feel intrusive. Existing accounts of personalization and privacy do not fully explain why these cues elicit opposing reactions. We treat Memory Boundary Fit (MBF) as a preliminary interaction-specific operationalization of whether remembered information appears to fall within a consumer's contextual boundary for the current exchange. Across six controlled, LLM-delivered chat experiments ( N = 2, 140), we compared three complete simulated message packages that differed in whether and how the assistant referenced remembered information: a relevant-memory cue, an intrusive-memory cue, and no memory reference. The assistant's memory references were fictitious claims rather than genuine retrieval of previously disclosed information. The principal and most consistent finding was that relevant-memory cue packages produced more favorable trust-related outcomes than intrusive-memory cue packages; comparisons with no memory varied across studies. Because the packages also differed in topical relevance, sensitivity, perceived usefulness, information source, and implied surveillance, the studies cannot isolate contextual fit, or any other single cue attribute, as the causal feature, and they do not establish MBF as a distinct psychological mechanism. Study 2 yielded same-session indirect associations consistent with the proposed MBF account. Across Study 2 and a supplemental validation sample, MBF explained additional variance in trust beyond that accounted for by the adjacent appraisals measured alongside it. However, all of these measures were self-reported in the same session. Study 3 found a larger intrusive-memory penalty in the complete sleep-health scenario than in the apparel scenario, but this is an exploratory scenario comparison rather than a test of information sensitivity. In Study 4, the specific editable dashboard tested increased average trust but did not selectively reduce the intrusive-memory penalty. Studies 5 and 6 extended the pattern to data-sharing and relational engagement, as well as to loyalty and opt-in intentions, but not to transactional engagement, which remained unaffected. These findings motivate contextual appropriateness as a candidate design consideration to be tested in real persistent-memory systems.

candidates.title: Innovative Training Approaches to Codevelop Digital Technologies to Foster Agroecological Practices: Insights from the OccitANum Living Lab
candidates.abstract: Digital technologies can strongly support agroecology transition of the agri-food system as they help optimise inputs, understand complex diversified systems, redesign agroecosystems, and connect farmers with citizens. But adoption remains low, largely due to poor adaptation to real needs, low digital literacy, and lack of trust. Living labs offer an interesting promise to better allow digital technologies use thanks to their structure based on participatory approaches and codesign of solutions with farmers in real-life conditions. Launched in 2020, OccitANum aims at this dual transition, agroecology via digital transformation. It is structured as an archipelago of 15 local Living labs grouped into 7 Open Labs by production sector (livestock, arable crops, vineyard, fruits, vegetables, beekeeping, local food supply) and supported by a central hub (CORE) providing services as facilitator training, data governance support, methodological tools, links with AgTech providers, evaluation frameworks. However, early results of OccitANum were limited because facilitators lacked skills in participatory design, digital maturity among farmers and advisors was low, farmers’ needs were misunderstood or poorly elicited, time and funding constraints hindered engagement. Therefore, to overcome these barriers, OccitANum pivoted toward capacity building through two main systems: (1) the MobiLab, a mobile fablab for hands-on digital learning travelling workshop enabling farmers to discover sensors, to prototype low-cost tools, and to build equipment themselves (so far over 500 participants, ~10 tools developed, dozens of prototypes built); (2) NUMAEE, a digital education for future farmers based on a “digital briefcase” for agricultural teachers to train students in building and using agricultural IoT tools and therefore increase confidence and practical understanding of digital technologies. Based on this momentum, two illustrative achievements are given: (a) the PiLowTech, a DIY soil moisture sensor co-designed with vegetable growers to improve irrigation and (b) the CentipOC network, a farmer-led initiative to deploy an open-source RTK geolocation network across multiple French departments, enabling affordable precision positioning and agriculture. These examples show how low-cost, accessible technologies can catalyse adoption and stimulate collective innovation dynamics. On a step forward, low-tech digital tools can greatly support On-Farm Experimentation, helping farmers test agroecological practices themselves and generate contextualised knowledge. In return, OFE provides real conditions to improve digital tools through iterative, bottom-up design. Thanks to OccitANum, we demonstrate that successful rural digitalisation is not primarily a technical challenge but an ecosystem challenge requiring sustained capacity building, long-term facilitation, alignment of actors, user-centred co-design practices, and tools adapted to real-world agroecological problems. Low-tech, DIY, and participatory approaches emerged as powerful levers to empower farmers and support both the digital and agroecological transitions.

candidates.title: Can you give me a hand? A case study of the effect of collaborative robot implementation from an operator perspective
candidates.abstract: Although the implementation of collaborative robots (cobots) in manufacturing has gained significant attention, few studies have examined the challenges operators face throughout the implementation process in real-life production contexts. In response, this study adopted a longitudinal design to investigate the implications of cobot implementation within a brownfield manufacturing setting across three distinct process phases: deployment initiation, operational testing and calibration, and full-scale integration. An exploratory case study was conducted at a Danish multinational company known for its measured approach to automation and strong commitment to job security, which helped reduce potential bias in assessing operators’ perspectives on automation. Data were collected through multiple rounds of semi-structured interviews, enabling the study to capture nuanced insights into operators’ evolving experiences over time. The results contribute to the literature by offering a detailed understanding of the human-centered dynamics of cobot integration, including safety, trust, communication and collaboration, which are critical for addressing implementation barriers. Furthermore, actionable recommendations for enhancing cobot adoption strategies in smart manufacturing are provided, emphasizing the importance of aligning technology integration with operator well-being and organizational practices.

candidates.title: Governing Human-Centric AI in Healthcare
candidates.abstract: The debate about artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare is no longer focused on whether AI will be used, but on how it should be governed. Across Europe and beyond, policymakers, healthcare organizations, and technology developers are searching for ways to ensure that AI systems remain accountable, transparent, and aligned with human values. The European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act represents one of the most ambitious attempts to address these challenges through a human-centric approach. Yet an important question remains unanswered: what does human-centric AI actually look like when organizations begin implementing AI technologies in practice? This book explores that question in the context of healthcare and humanoid robotics. Rather than examining regulation or technology in isolation, it brings together perspectives from AI governance, management, healthcare, and technology acceptance research. The discussion moves from the principles embedded in the AI Act to the realities of organizational decision-making, showing how ideas such as human dignity, human oversight, trust, inclusivity, and accountability influence the adoption of emerging technologies. A central theme running throughout the book is the gap between technological possibility and organizational readiness. Drawing on empirical research involving 527 respondents – current and future decision-makers, the book examines perceptions of humanoid robots in healthcare and identifies the factors that encourage or discourage their adoption. The findings reveal that acceptance is shaped not only by expected benefits but also by concerns about trust, responsibility, ethics, patient safety, and the preservation of human interaction in care. The book also proposes two original concepts: the Human-Centric Robot Acceptance Index (HCRAI), which evaluates readiness for humanoid robot adoption, and the Risk Gradient Model of Humanoid Robot Task Acceptance, which explains why some healthcare tasks are considered more suitable for robots than others. Together, these contributions offer new ways of understanding how AI technologies can be integrated into healthcare organizations while maintaining meaningful human oversight. Written for researchers, healthcare professionals, managers, policymakers, and students, this book provides an interdisciplinary perspective on one of the most important challenges facing contemporary healthcare: ensuring that technological innovation remains centered on people rather than technology itself.

candidates.title: Mechanism of AI chatbot anthropomorphism on consumer impulse buying in live streaming scenarios based on SOR framework
candidates.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) is integrated into real-time e-commerce, it is necessary to study how AI virtual hosts affect consumers' immediate purchase decisions. This research is based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and explores the psychological mechanism by which the characteristics of AI hosts influence impulsive purchases. The scenario-based experiments show that AI anthropomorphism (ANT) and social conversation cues (SCC) affect impulsive purchases through two mediating states: cognitive trust and emotional arousal. The results indicate that the association between SCC and trust and arousal is stronger than that of visual anthropomorphism, and multiple group analyses show that this mechanism is roughly consistent across gender groups, but there are differences between the product participation and AI experience groups. This research expands upon previous work by testing visual and verbal anthropomorphic cues as parallel stimuli in live-streaming business, and provides guidance for the design of AI virtual hosts.

candidates.title: Sustainability cost of defect engineering in color centers for quantum communications
candidates.abstract: Quantum communication relies on optically active color centers for scalable spin-photon networking, yet the sustainability implications of defect engineering remain largely unexplored. We comparatively evaluate twenty host crystal-defect generation combinations across diamond, SiC, h-BN, GaN, ZnO using ion implantation, e-beam irradiation, laser writing, and heteroepitaxial growth techniques. A multi-attribute cradle-to-gate framework integrating life cycle, chemical hazard, human health toxicity, and technoeconomic assessments reveals distinct thermodynamic, chemical, health, and economic tradeoffs emerge across defect engineering pathways. h-BN paired with laser writing shows the lowest overall burdens, with low energy demand, global warming potential <20 kg CO2 eq./chip, minimal hazard/toxicity profiles, and lowest fabrication cost. SiC provides a balanced near-term pathway by retaining strong quantum functionality while moderating sustainability burdens. ZnO and GaN show selective process-level advantages for integrated photonics, whereas diamond remains burden-intensive due to energy-demanding growth and complex post-defect stabilization requirements. Identified greener interventions enable scalable and resource-conscious quantum communication hardware. Sustainable manufacturing is becoming an increasingly important consideration for emerging quantum technologies. Here, the authors assess the environmental, chemical, human-health, and economic impacts of defect engineering strategies for color-center platforms used in quantum communications, highlighting trade-offs between quantum functionality and resource demands while identifying lower-impact solutions.

candidates.title: Loneliness to consumption intention: emotional bonding and escapism in AI emotional companion app use
candidates.abstract: With the diffusion of generative AI, AI emotional companion apps have emerged as a new domain of digital consumption in which users may pay to extend relationship-like experiences. This study examines how loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy are associated with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention through two competing pathways: emotional bonding with the AI (relational compensation) and escapism (avoidant compensation). The emotional bond with the AI is modeled as a second-order construct comprising anthropomorphism, emotional responsiveness, and parasocial intimacy. Data were collected from 393 adult users in China who used AI emotional companion apps at least twice per week and were analyzed using structural equation modeling. Loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy were positively associated with both emotional bonding and escapism. However, significant indirect associations with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention emerged only through the emotional-bond pathway. Direct comparisons further showed that the relational indirect effects were significantly stronger than the avoidant indirect effects across all antecedent–outcome combinations. Escapism was significantly associated with both outcomes when modeled alone but became nonsignificant when emotional bonding was included, suggesting that its association with consumer responses largely overlaps with the relational pathway. A partial-mediation analysis further showed that actual-ideal self-discrepancy retained a significant direct association with continuance intention. These findings suggest that relational compensation, rather than avoidant compensation, is more closely associated with willingness to pay for experience enhancement and intention to continue using AI companions. The study extends compensatory-use, self-discrepancy, and parasocial-interaction perspectives to the AI-companion context by linking psychological vulnerability to experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention, while highlighting implications for responsible relational design and user protection.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Anxiety, Impostor Phenomenon, and Workplace Deviant Behavior Among Nurses: A Three Wave Longitudinal Study
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: The widespread application of artificial intelligence technologies in healthcare has intensified nurses' perceptions of technological replacement and role uncertainty, making artificial intelligence anxiety an increasingly important occupational psychological risk factor. The impostor phenomenon may play a critical mediating role between anxiety and workplace deviant behavior; however, longitudinal evidence remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine the dynamic relationship between artificial intelligence anxiety and workplace deviant behavior among nurses, and to test the longitudinal mediating role of the impostor phenomenon. METHODS: A three wave longitudinal design was employed to conduct a 6-month longitudinal survey among 594 clinical nurses. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the longitudinal relationships among the study variables. RESULT: Across the three waves, artificial intelligence anxiety, impostor phenomenon, and workplace deviant behavior were significantly correlated. Longitudinal mediation analyses indicated that artificial intelligence anxiety had a significant direct effect on subsequent workplace deviant behavior and that the impostor phenomenon significantly mediated the relationship between artificial intelligence anxiety at T1 and workplace deviant behavior at T3. LINKING EVIDENCE TO ACTION: Establishing routine monitoring and early-warning mechanisms for technology-related psychological stress, together with personalized support strategies that enhance perceived technological control and reinforce the core values of humanistic nursing care, may effectively reduce nurses' cognitive distortions and mitigate workplace deviant behavior.

candidates.title: “Serve Them with Rituals”: Power and Emotions in the Confucian Parent-Child Relationship
candidates.abstract: This article challenges the conventional portrayal of the parent-child relationship in Confucian thought as authoritarian and even oppressive. It reconstructs a Confucian ethical view of the relationship from the perspective of parenting in addition to the more common discussions of filial conduct. It argues that the Analects ’ view of filial conduct emphasizes following ritual norms instead of absolute obedience to parents. Although the Analects does not explicitly discuss parenting, passages that mention Confucius with his children are thought provoking. By examining the role of emotions and power dynamics in rituals involving the parent-child relationship, the article defends an account of how Confucian ritual cultivates appropriate love and respect on the part of both parents and children, and its intention is to restrain the conduct of the more powerful in such unequal relationships, instead of oppressing the vulnerable.

candidates.title: Gaze-Anchored Social Net: Decoding Implicit Relations via Joint Modeling
Mapping of Power and Privacy: A Study on Domestic Surveillance and Power in Select Malayalam Cinema
candidates.abstract: The idea of surveillance is not new to the world and its people. The history of surveillance dates back to the history of human civilization. Surveillance is closely associated with power, the one who can see everything can be powerful above all. The one who knows everything is the one who holds the power. Foucault in Discipline and Punish: The Birth of the Prison explains that since the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Western societies can be defined by a new form of power that is capillary and affects ‘the grain of individuals, touches their bodies and inserts itself into their actions and attitudes, their discourses, learning processes and everyday lives’ (Foucault 39). In simpler terms, the Surveillance is active in all systems of life, and these systems often remain hidden or unnoticed, precisely because they are found in the fibres of daily life, which is what makes them so powerful and ubiquitous. This paper tries to analyse the aspects of surveillance and its association with power in the Malayali household through the movies Android Kunjappan version 5.25 (2019) directed by Ratheesh Bhaskara Poduval and Ottamuri Velicham (2017) directed by Rahul Riji Nair. Both the movies represent the micro surveillance within the family and the hold of power between the characters of the movies. The paper tries to point out the system of power and surveillance using a close examination of the plot and character motifs identified through a comparative study.

candidates.title: EIGR-infer: a blockchain-governed framework for decentralised LLM inference via encrypted intent-guided routing, semantic sharding, and four novel privacy mechanisms
candidates.abstract: Abstract The dominance of centralized cloud providers in large language model (LLM) inference compels users to transmit sensitive queries to third-party servers, sacrificing data privacy and introducing systemic single points of failure. This paper presents EIGR-Infer —a decentralised inference framework that distributes LLM execution across a heterogeneous peer-to-peer (P2P) mesh of consumer-grade edge devices including smartphones, laptops, and local GPU workstations. The framework’s foundational contribution is the encrypted intent-guided routing (EIGR) protocol, which resolves the Finder’s Dilemma: how to direct a query to the semantically appropriate model shard without revealing the query’s content to the routing network. EIGR achieves this through three coordinated mechanisms: on-device semantic intent hashing using HKDF-SHA256 over a local cosine-similarity projection, Kademlia-DHT-based expert shard discovery keyed on the non-invertible hash, and chaos-adaptive onion routing for encrypted delivery. Beyond EIGR, this paper introduces four entirely novel, previously unpublished contributions: (1) DP-SSIM, a Differentially private semantic intent mapping construction providing formal $$(\varepsilon ,\delta )$$ -DP guarantees on routing metadata; (2) the ghost shard protocol (GSP), a deceptive defence mechanism using cryptographically indistinguishable fake shard announcements to deter and detect model-extraction adversaries; (3) federated domain centroid consensus (FDCC), a Byzantine-fault-tolerant gossip protocol for maintaining the shared domain vocabulary without any central authority; and (4) session-adaptive shard re-routing (SASR), a mid-session semantic drift detection and shard migration mechanism for high-quality private multi-turn inference. All seven algorithms are formally specified and analysed. Discrete-event simulation across a 1000-node heterogeneous mesh demonstrates EIGR discovery latency of 47 ms at the 95th percentile, end-to-end inference latency of 460 ms for 512-token prompts, DP-SSIM overhead below 2 ms, ghost shard detection rate of 98.3%, FDCC convergence within 3–4 gossip rounds, and SASR re-routing latency of 31 ms—all compatible with interactive inference targets.

Integrating socio-emotional scaffolding into educational robotics: Effects on classroom climate in heterogeneous lower secondary schools
candidates.abstract: This study explores the impact of educational robotics activities explicitly designed to foster collaboration and inclusion on classroom climate. A quasi-experimental design was implemented in two rural schools, involving 47 students aged 11–12. The experimental group engaged in robotics sessions enriched with socio-emotional scaffolding, while the control group participated in technically comparable but socially neutral activities. Data were collected using the Classroom Climate Questionnaire and a student feedback survey. Results showed a significant improvement in perceived classroom climate in the experimental group, contrasted with a decline in the control group. Qualitative findings further revealed that experimental students described their experiences in a more competent way, without referring to frustration. These outcomes highlight the importance of embedding socio-emotional learning objectives into technology-enhanced instruction.

candidates.abstract: Makerspace is a very innovative concept for present library services. Various core usages along with specific tools and activities of makerspace in university libraries were discussed to encourage nascent users with hands on real-world knowledge thereby enhancing library role beyond traditional books and database. An intrinsic mechanism has been developed to create a diversified space for variable users. Based on the extracted data from makerspace.com various websites key features of makerspace in USA, China and India were briefed along with the services provided to the users in tabulated format for better understanding. Several pros and corns were dealt with while assembling a diversified makerspace. It was found that most conceptualised makerspace in the United States of America due to advancement in technology while China had few makerspace implemented due to their dependency on the Government whereas India genuinely flourished in the area of education research and innovation with comprehensive makerspace concept.

candidates.title: Food at the Hearth: Emotional Connections and Generational Transmission of Escudella i Carn d'Olla in Traditional Catalan Cuisine
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper analyses the changes and continuity in the preparation and rituals of escudella i carn d'olla , a manifestation of traditional Catalan cuisine. Based on interviews with 27 ordinary citizens from different generations, the research explores how they experience, elaborate, and emotionally relate to escudella i carn d'olla , and what generational and gender patterns can be identified in these relationships. Results show that one of the most notable aspects of escudella i carn d'olla is its role in family bonding, which is shared by the three generations—the dish as a symbol of a family ritual, which mostly happens in winter, and creates a shared feeling of warmth. In addition, the changing pace of life and new consumption patterns affect how family cooking is perceived and practiced. While for older generations, the preparation of escudella is an act of caring and love for the family, younger generations have lost interest in dedicating so much time to preparing it. Its traditional preparation reflects local supply systems—such as local butcher shops and markets—and embodies a female know‐how. Its value lies in its emotional significance as it represents a cultural and social connection to the past and the present, but also to the future.

candidates.title: Predictions and goals modulate use of partner's gaze during joint action with humanoid robots
candidates.abstract: During joint actions, partners coordinate attention and actions by using each other's gaze to predict upcoming actions and align with shared goals. Although gaze orienting has been extensively studied using screen-based paradigms, it remains unclear whether partner reliability and action goals calibrate the use of the partner's gaze during embodied interactions. We addressed this using a humanoid robot as a co-actor in two experiments. In Experiment 1, participants performed a color-sorting task while the robot provided informative or noninformative gaze cues. Cue reliability was manipulated between participants: one group experienced a robot whose gaze was informative in 80% of trials, and another at chance level. Task difficulty was manipulated within participants. Only the reliable group made fewer errors on valid than invalid trials under high-difficulty. In Experiment 2, participants completed a handover task in which an auditory cue established an action plan, the robot looked toward a goal-congruent or incongruent object, and a target appeared at a valid or invalid location. Participants responded faster at the cued location only when the robot looked toward the goal-matching object, with eye tracking confirming covert attentional shifts. Together, these findings show that the use of the partner's gaze in embodied joint action operates as a flexible, utility-weighting heuristic. Observers weighted gaze according to its value, upweighting gaze from a reliable partner and when it aligned with shared goals and down-weighting gaze that conflicted with predictions. These results advance understanding of gaze use as a predictive, context-dependent mechanism with implications for reliance on social signals during joint action with humans and artificial agents.

candidates.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Surgical vs. Conservative Management of Chronic Anal Fissures
candidates.abstract: Background. Chronic anal fissure is highly prevalent, and the decision to undertake pharmacological sphincter relaxation (SR) versus lateral internal sphincterotomy (LIS) remains a matter of debate. While the short-term healing rates are well established, the long-term outcomes greater than two years and the relationship with continence are less predictable. Aim. To compare long-term healing, recurrence, pain, continence, quality of life, and patient satisfaction following surgical versus conservative management of adult patients with chronic anal fissure, and to elucidate predictors of long-term treatment failure. Methods. Using a cross-sectional design, a tertiary colorectal unit identified all adult patients treated for chronic anal fissure from 01/01/25 until 31/3/26. Patients were followed up with history, clinical examination, a visual analogue scale for pain, the Wexner score for anal incontinence, the Euro Qol 5D 5L (EQ-5D-5L), and an interview by a colorectal surgeon unfamiliar with the index intervention. Statistical analysis employed the independent samples t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, Chi-square or Fisher's exact test, and binary logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results. The mean (standard deviation) age of patients was 38.6 (11.2) years and 34.2 (7.9) months from intervention. Both groups were comparable at baseline. Long-term healing rates were greater with LIS at 71/78 (91.0%) vs. 52/81 (64.2%) SR patients ( 2.30-13.91, 7.558.66 OR, p < 0.001), and there was less recurrence at 7.7% versus 38.3% ( 2.80-203.08, 20.80OR, p < 0.001) and crossover or re-intervention rates at 5.1% versus 27.2% (p < 0.001). Pain at follow-up was less after LIS at VAS 1.2 (1.1) vs. 2.6 (1.8) ( 2.31, 6.946.94, p < 0.001), while EQ-5D-5L scores were better at 0.89 (0.09) vs. 0.81 (0.13) ( 2.94, 5.414.21, p < 0.001). The rate of any continence disturbance was higher after LIS at 11.5% (9/78) versus 2.5% (2/81) (p = 0.030); however, these were limited to slight soiling or flatus, and there was no incontinence to solid stool. Multivariate logistic regression revealed conservative management (1.09-5.11, 2.48-11.79, p < 0.001), persistent constipation (1.32-6.55, 2.94, p = 0.009), and duration of symptoms > 1 year (1.09-5.11, 2.36, p = 0.011) independently predicted long-term failure. Conclusion. Although sphincterotomy provided significantly greater and more durable resolution of symptoms than medical therapy at a mean follow-up of 38 months, the residual risk of a minor continence disturbance was low. Conservative management remains appropriate; however, those with chronicity or untreated constipation should be made aware that definitive intervention is unavoidable.

candidates.title: Automated detection of mutual gaze in mobile eye-tracking studies of multi-party interactions
candidates.abstract: This article describes a data-processing pipeline for quantifying mutual gaze in mobile eye-tracking studies. Mutual gaze is defined as eye contact between participants who look at each other simultaneously. We applied the pipeline to data from dyadic and multi-party interactions (“quartets”). Using state-of-the-art computer vision tools for fiducial-marker tracking and face detection, the pipeline processes scene camera videos from TobiiPro eye-trackers to extract facial areas-of-interest (AOIs). Each participant's gaze samples are classified relative to visible co-participants, indicating when gaze is directed at another's face. By integrating multiple participants' high-resolution data streams, the pipeline identifies periods of unreciprocated (unilateral) gaze as well as mutual gaze. The output files contain time-stamped measures of gaze events and can be imported into the annotation tool ELAN for qualitative analysis. While processing is largely automated, some steps require validity checks by the researcher. To underpin our observations on the potential of the proposed pipeline for the automatic extraction of mutual gaze, we subsequently conduct an exploratory analysis on the participants' unilateral gaze and mutual gaze proportions in relation to the following factors: seating position, speaking proportion, age, gender, familiarity, and movement synchrony. The results show that speaking proportion, seating position, and familiarity were significantly associated with unilateral and mutual gaze proportion. By contrast, an association with age, gender, and movement synchrony measurements was not shown. The article concludes with a critical discussion of the limitations and strengths of the proposed pipeline. We highlight the opportunities and challenges of quantifying gaze patterns in complex multi-party settings with a specific interest on how existing qualitative and quantitative findings may be brought together for future studies.

candidates.title: The context of AI transformation: perceptions of AI ethicality and their impact on trust and use intentions
candidates.abstract: Introduction: As the implementation of AI accelerates within organizations, concerns emerge about the ethicality of AI-driven systems and tools and the ways people use them. Although previous literature proposes numerous theories regarding how to develop and use AI ethically, questions remain about how users perceive the ethicality of AI and the effects this has on their engagement with AI tools. The study aims to explore whether and how certain perceptions of AI tool attributes, including beliefs about the explainability of the AI tool (xAI) and moral intensity dimensions (i.e., magnitude of consequences and proximity), influence perceptions of AI ethicality. Additionally, the study examines the effects of AI ethicality perceptions on the likelihood to recommend AI tools and functionality trust in AI. Methods: Researchers employ a randomized, controlled study design to investigate the relationships between the antecedents, perceptions of AI ethicality, and outcomes of functionality trust and behavioral intention. Results: Analyses revealed that AI ethicality perceptions significantly mediated the relationship between xAI and the likelihood to recommend the AI tool, whereas functionality trust in the AI tool significantly mediated the relationship between proximity and the likelihood to recommend the AI tool. Discussion: The results indicate the strength of users' beliefs about xAI on their perceptions of AI ethicality and how users perceive AI as less capable of making decisions for human decision recipients. The perceptual nature of the study provides a theoretical contribution to the growing body of AI-related research relevant to organizations. The findings also offer a perspective to organizations implementing AI tools, signaling the need for management to consider context and ethical perceptions when implementing AI tools in the workplace.

candidates.title: Collective capacity building for emotionally charged work: a grounded theory of strategies for maintaining meaning and well-being in emotionally charged work
candidates.abstract: PURPOSE: Emotionally charged work-encompassing emotional demands and emotional labour - has been associated with ill health and alienation. While the consequences of such work has been widely theorized, the prevention of negative consequences remains undertheorized. METHODS: In this study, we adopt a classical grounded theory approach to (a) Explore the main concern of employed people regarding emotionally charged work and (b) Generate a grounded theory that could inform sustainable organization of emotionally charged work and the prevention of compassion fatigue. Initial purposeful sampling included eight employees and managers from psychiatric hospitals. As subsequent theoretical sampling required broader diversity, we conducted interviews with 15 additional participants across varied occupations, including ministers of religion, military personnel, social care workers, educators, IT managers, and others. RESULTS: Using open coding and constant comparison, we developed a grounded theory of collective capacity building for emotionally charged work. We found that the main concern of participants was to maintain meaningful working lives and in the context of emotionally charged work, they achieved this by building collective capacity for this work. CONCLUSION: Our findings offer theoretical and practical guidance for sustainably organizing work in occupations marked by high levels of emotionally charged work.
